Rules / Design

SK6008 An extension method extends object

The method appears in completion for every value, even though almost no extension is meaningful for every type.

CategoryDesign
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

An extension method is an API surface projected onto its receiver type. Using object projects it onto every string, integer, collection, task and domain value in the program, making completion noisier and making accidental calls easy. A narrower receiver also states the contract the implementation already relies on. There is no mechanical fix: selecting that receiver is an API-design decision.

Example

Instead of:

public static string Dump(this object value) => value.ToString()!;

Write:

public static string Dump(this SyntaxNode value) => value.ToString();

When it does not fire

A deliberately universal operation can be valid, especially diagnostics and serialization helpers. The rule reports only a resolved System.Object receiver on a real extension method; dynamic, a user type named Object, ordinary object parameters and narrower receivers are ignored. Suppress or baseline the rare API that is intentionally universal.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK6008.severity
